Checking tools, inputs/outputs, dependencies and budget

master_plan.title: Per-Class Accuracy Impact of Basic Image Augmentation on Fashion-MNIST Garment Categories

agents.name: Code Engineer
agents.instructions: Set up the Python environment and implement all model and training code. Write SmallCNN in src/model.py with exactly three conv blocks 1→32→64→128 (3×3 kernels, padding=1, BatchNorm, ReLU, MaxPool) plus FC head (256 units, 0.5 dropout, 10-class output) and a set_seed() covering random/numpy/torch/cuda/cudnn. Implement src/train.py with train_epoch(), evaluate(), and run_training() including epoch-level checkpoints for crash recovery and CSV logging. Validate all code with dummy forward passes and a one-epoch smoke test before marking tasks complete.

agents.name: Data Engineer
agents.instructions: Download Fashion-MNIST via torchvision and configure both transform pipelines. Define no_aug as ToTensor+Normalize(0.2860,0.3530) and aug as RandomHorizontalFlip(p=0.5)+RandomAffine(degrees=10,translate=(0.1,0.1))+ToTensor+Normalize. Save dataset statistics to JSON and produce a visual grid of sample images under both pipelines. Post class-name-to-label mapping and dataset split sizes to team notes.

agents.name: GPU Training Engineer
agents.instructions: Write scripts/gpu_train.py to run all four training configurations sequentially on CUDA, then submit via run_gpu_jobs as a single job to minimise queue overhead. After job completion verify all 12 output files exist and are non-empty. Post GPU device name, CUDA version, and per-run test accuracies to team notes as execution evidence.

agents.name: Statistical Analyst
agents.instructions: Validate prediction files for completeness and accuracy consistency, compute per-class precision/recall/F1/accuracy using scikit-learn, derive delta metrics with seed-level ranges, and run Spearman rank correlation between morphological symmetry labels and delta-accuracy with 5000-resample bootstrap CIs. Frame all per-class findings as exploratory relative to the approximately 1.5pp binomial noise floor and flag any model with overall accuracy below 85% with an explicit caveat.

agents.name: Visualization Engineer
agents.instructions: Merge learning curves into long-format CSV, compute row-normalised confusion matrices and the delta confusion matrix, then produce all three publication-quality figures (300 dpi) and two LaTeX booktabs tables. Use matplotlib/seaborn with exact color and format specifications from the plan. T5.3 can start as soon as T3.2 completes independently of T4.x work.

agents.name: Results Compiler
agents.instructions: Read all analysis outputs and compile results/SUMMARY.md with every key number: overall test accuracy per seed and condition, delta-accuracy per class with seed ranges, Spearman rho with 95% CI, max off-diagonal delta in confusable-tops group, and paths to all figures and tables. Every claim must cite a specific numeric value traceable to an upstream analysis file.

master_plan.summary: Six agents cooperate to train SmallCNN on Fashion-MNIST under no-augmentation and augmentation conditions (seeds 42/123) and decompose accuracy by garment class. A1 implements model and training code (T1.1, T1.3, T1.4) while A2 configures data pipelines (T1.2) concurrently; A3 submits all four GPU training runs in a single run_gpu_jobs call (T2.1); A4 validates outputs and computes per-class metrics and Spearman symmetry correlation (T3.1, T4.1, T4.3); A5 merges learning curves, computes confusion matrices, and produces all figures and tables (T3.2, T4.2, T5.1–T5.4); A6 compiles all key numbers into results/SUMMARY.md (T6.1). Parallelism is maximised at three points: T1.2 and T1.3 after T1.1, T3.1 and T3.2 after T2.1, and T4.1 and T4.2 after T3.1.

datasets.name: Fashion-MNIST
datasets.notes: 70,000 grayscale 28×28 images: 60,000 train plus 10,000 test, balanced 1,000 per class across 10 garment categories. Use torch.utils.data.random_split on the 60k training set with a seeded Generator for 54k/6k train/val split. Normalization constants mean=0.2860, std=0.3530 are accepted dataset-wide values.
datasets.format: IDX binary (ubyte); torchvision returns tensors of shape (1,28,28) with integer labels 0–9
datasets.access_method: torchvision.datasets.FashionMNIST(root='data/fashion_mnist', download=True) — no authentication required; torchvision fetches IDX gzip files from Zalando S3 mirror automatically

checkpoints.reason: Human review of GPU training outputs: verify all 12 files are present, overall test accuracy is plausible (>=85% for no_aug condition on at least one seed), and training logs show convergence. Gate before expensive per-class analysis.

Human review of all publication figures and tables before final summary: confirm figures are publication-quality, per-class delta values are interpretable, and LaTeX tables render correctly with booktabs style.

execution_notes: T1.2 and T1.3 run concurrently after T1.1 (A2 and A1 in parallel) with no dependency between them.
T3.1 and T3.2 run concurrently after T2.1 (A4 and A5 in parallel); T4.1 and T4.2 run concurrently after T3.1.
T5.3 depends only on T3.2 and can proceed independently of T4.x tasks; T5.1 requires T4.3 which requires T4.1.
All four training runs are packed into a single run_gpu_jobs call to avoid repeated queue delays; sequential execution within one GPU session is expected to take 40-50 minutes total.

The plan's T6.1 paper-draft task is replaced with a results/SUMMARY.md compilation task per blueprint rules; the Report stage handles full paper writing from this summary and the figure and table artifacts.
If torch.cuda.is_available() returns False during T2.1 GPU job execution, the script raises RuntimeError before any training begins so the job fails fast; A3 should check the log and retry.

Fashion-MNIST normalization constants mean=0.2860 and std=0.3530 are dataset-wide standard values; the slight distribution shift from the 6k validation holdout is negligible and does not require recomputation from the 54k split.
No MATLAB or non-pip tools are required; all methods are implemented with PyTorch, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, scipy, and pandas.
